title: doorman environment variables
description: Secrets and tuning. Loaded by systemd's EnvironmentFile in production and by `make run` in development. Names and defaults match examples/.env.example exactly.

ARI_ALLOW_REMOTE.description: Permit a non-loopback ARI host. doorman refuses to start otherwise, because ARI is full call control behind a plaintext password. The one documented exception is running off-box over a tailnet — never the LAN.

ARI_APP.description: Stasis application name. Must match Stasis(...) in asterisk/extensions.conf.

ARI_BASE_URL.description: Asterisk ARI base URL. Keep ARI bound to loopback; doorman runs on the same host.

x-rules: Required. doorman refuses to start without it.
Required. doorman refuses to start without it.

CALL_LOG_MAX_BYTES.description: Rotate the call log at this size, keeping one previous generation. Twenty calls a day is roughly 2 MB a year, so this cap is for the case that is not twenty calls a day.

CALL_LOG_PATH.description: Enables the per-call record log, one JSON line per completed call. Empty (the default) means no call log. Unlike the operational log this file holds full caller IDs — which is what makes "who called while I was out" answerable — so it is created 0600 and belongs on the box. Read it with `doorman calls`, which redacts by default. Written off the call path: a full buffer drops records and counts them rather than delaying a call. Nothing on the call path ever reads it back; it is an output, not state.

DEFAULT_COUNTRY_CODE.description: Country code assumed when a caller ID arrives without one.

EXTENSION_LENGTH.description: Digits in an extension when PIN lengths are mixed.

FIRST_DIGIT_TIMEOUT_MS.description: Time to dial the FIRST digit, measured from the end of the greeting. Generous on purpose: a stranger reading a PIN off a card needs longer than a stopwatch allows.

LOG_REDACT_CALLER_ID.description: Redact caller IDs in logs, keeping only a fragment. On by default: the caller attribute rides on every line a call produces, and journals get shipped and backed up. Setting this false is a deliberate debugging opt-out — see CLAUDE.md invariant 1.

MAX_CONCURRENT_CALLS.description: Ceiling on simultaneous inbound calls. The rate limit counts failures per caller and cannot see a flood from many numbers, which would keep every handset ringing. Excess calls are hung up without ringing anything. 0 disables.

MAX_PIN_ATTEMPTS.description: Wrong-PIN retries allowed within one call before dismissal.

POLICY_WATCH.description: Re-read both config files on change so edits go live without a restart. An invalid file is rejected and the previous policy stays in service.

PROMPT_MEDIA_PREFIX.description: Asterisk media prefix, NOT a filesystem path. Files live in /var/lib/asterisk/sounds/<prefix>/. Also how a prompt pack is swapped in.

RATELIMIT_ENABLED.description: After repeated failures a caller skips the greeting entirely and goes straight to dismissal, leaving nothing to brute-force against.

RATELIMIT_MAX_FAILURES.description: Failures from one number inside the window before that caller is dismissed without a greeting.

RING_TIMEOUT_S.description: How long the house rings before giving up.

x-rules: Every problem is reported at once — doorman does not make you fix env vars one restart at a time.
HANDSET_<NAME>_PASSWORD variables are named by password_env in handsets.toml and read by `doorman render`, not by the daemon.
The VOICEMAIL_*, STT_*, and SMTP_* keys in examples/.env.example are reserved for the unshipped voicemail feature. They are deliberately not read yet, so .env will not churn when it lands.
